name: Bybit linear BTCUSDT perpetual mark momentum
description: Causal simple basis-point returns of the Bybit linear BTCUSDT perpetual mark price from the tickers stream (merged partial updates), sampled once per second off the decision clock, over 10-second, 1-minute, 5-minute and 15-minute horizons. return_bps_10s, return_bps_1m, return_bps_5m and return_bps_15m are 10000 times the mark change over the horizon divided by the mark 10, 60, 300 and 900 seconds earlier on the one-second ring. direction_5m is down, flat or up from the full-precision five-minute return, with flat exactly zero and no dead band. Ready output requires 901 contiguous one-second samples (the longest horizon, 15 minutes) of the mark; each one-second sample holds the venue's latest mark row for up to a 3-second bound (a research default that admits the sub-1 Hz mark cadence, the premium-index poll landing about every 1.3 seconds and Bybit mark prices carrying multi-second gaps), and a mark row 3 seconds or more old — a stalled poll or an absent mark — is a missing observation that breaks continuity and restarts the warm-up (no gap bridging). Warm-up degrades as bybit_warming_up, a stale merged mark as bybit_stale and a mark-missing feed state as bybit_recovery_required. The Bybit linear lane refuses to start (exit 78) unless SIGNALS_ENABLED_VENUES lists bybit; the rights gate is a startup refusal, never an instance status. This identity is reference-free and scale-free: it publishes no price-denominated field, only basis-point returns and their root mean square, so nothing is converted from USDT to USD. There is no usdt_usd_rate, no usdt_usd_rate_age_ms and no usdt_reference_stale gating; returns are quote-neutral by construction. quote_currency is the constant "usd". Decimal outputs are rounded to eight places using round-half-to-even.
